doc.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Arranging and style in the Basie band
title: Wess's flute, Foster's arranging, and sharing the writing
summary: Wess reintroduced flute while Foster contributed arrangements; Wess, Hefti and Thad Jones also wrote.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I know part of the traditional Basie band was a contrast in the saxophones between the two tenors. That manifested itself for you in the Basie band in a number of kind of contrasts and with different players, but it seems like you explored this really with Frank, not so much always with two tenors, but just the notion of matching your different instruments, flutes and alto and the different things. Maybe you could talk about that and also maybe talk about or comment on whether or not the difference in how you are as people finds itself in how you play.

He had an extra dimension in that flute. He’s credited with reintroducing the flute into jazz, which is to say that he wasn’t the first flutist to play jazz, but it had been years before. It had been way back in the late ’30s, I think, when a gentleman by the name of Wayman Carver played the flute, but I never heard any recordings by this Mr. Carver. I don’t even recall with whom he played.

Chick Webb, okay. There were a great number of years in which the flute was not heard of after Carver’s presentation of it. Frank Wess reintroduced it, and it became a very, very popular instrument, as you all know. He was very proficient on the flute. He wasn’t just -- it wasn’t something he just picked up and started playing. He had been working on the flute. He was an excellent flautist, so he had that dimension going for him. My extra dimension was my composing and arranging. In that area I contributed widely to the band, which is not to downplay the fact that Frank Wess himself is an excellent composer-arranger. Some of the most wonderful music to come out of the band was composed and arranged by Frank Wess. I’m speaking of a song by the name of Half Moon Street and another song called Summer Frost. There were other songs that probably didn’t gain too much prominence, because Neil Hefti’s arrangements and some of mine -- and Thad Jones was also another heavy contributor, by way of arranging, to the band’s repertoire.
